newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Royal event draws big crowds. Heavy rain could do nothing to dampen the blaze and glory of yesterday's Royal Barge Procession which delighted thousands of spectators. Thais and foreigners crammed both banks of the Chao Phyaya River hours before the tradtional pageant began and were not disappointed with what they saw. Fifty-two barges crewed by 2,082 men dressed in glorious costumes rowed past in celebration of His Majesty the King's Golden Jubilee. (BANGKOK POST)

- Rayong depot chemical blast claims 12 lives. At least 12 people were killed and 17 injured yesterday in a fire following an explosion at an illegal petroleum depot, police said. Police and witnesses said the death poll could be higher because about another dozen people may have been trapped by the blaze in Puak Daeng district. (THE NATION)

- Seven foreign banks gain full branch licences. The finance Ministry yesterday granted full-branch licences to seven foreign banks, which were selected by the Bank of Thailand to upgrade their offshore banking units. The seven banks are Bank of Nova Scotia, Germany-based Dresdner Bank, France-based Banque National de Paris, the Industrial Bank of Japan, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, Sumitomo Bank and the Bank of China. (BANGKOK POST)

- Sitca Investment & Securities-led consortium has won preliminary approval from the Bank of Thailand to rescue the Bankok Bank of Commerce, due mainly to a superior proposal concerning bad debts. Sitca Chairman Anan Anantrakul said the consortium, compromising nine parties which joined Sitca's failed attempt to bid for a banking licence, will start due dilegence on Nov 11. (THE NATION)
